svg.title: Visual abstract: Automated somatic SNV calling in breast cancer
svg.desc: A Snakemake pipeline following GATK Best Practices calls somatic SNVs in two breast cancer tumor and matched-normal pairs (HCC1143, HCC1954) on GRCh38: FastQC, BWA-MEM, Samtools, Picard, BQSR, Mutect2 with gnomAD and a panel of normals, contamination-aware filtering, then VAF, TMB and coverage metrics. It found 102 PASS somatic mutations on chr17 with low contamination.
svg.text: VISUAL ABSTRACT · CANCER GENOMICS · SNAKEMAKE · GATK BEST PRACTICES
Automated somatic SNV calling in breast cancer
Tumor vs matched-normal exomes from two breast cancer cell lines, from raw reads to filtered VCF
HCC1143 and HCC1954, each with a matched normal
Somatic mutations exist only in tumor
cells. Therefore, each tumor is read
gnomAD and a panel of normals remove
HCC1954 starts from raw FASTQ, while
Contamination stays low in both pairs.
TMB divides PASS calls by an assumed
exome size and is illustrative only.
Snakemake DAG run in WSL2 with Bioconda, packaged with a Dockerfile
One Snakemake command takes a tumor and normal pair from raw reads to a filtered somatic VCF, then
reports VAF, TMB and coverage. As a result, any new pair follows the same reproducible, containerized path.
